name: Create Agent
description:
Creates a new agent at g/<agentId> in the caller's namespace. The name must be unused; an existing agent is an error. To replace an agent, explicitly call agent:delete with remove=true and then create the new agent. Use agent:update for history-preserving config or state changes.

Omit config for the recommended skilled default: bounded inspect plus read/list tools and skills loaded on demand, using the venue's default transition and LLM operation. Pass config={} only when you intentionally want an explicit minimal configuration.

Config may be one inline map, one reference, or an ordered array of either. Ordered layers merge left-to-right: nested maps merge recursively and every later scalar/array value overrides the earlier value. Example: config=['v/agents/templates/worker', {llmOperation:'v/models/anthropic/claude-sonnet-5'}]. References may point to flat config maps or canonical Covia assets carrying an agent.config facet.

The 'operation' field must be a resolvable lattice path (e.g. 'v/ops/llmagent/chat' for plain persona chat, 'v/ops/goaltree/chat' for goal-decomposing planners) — bare adapter shorthand like 'llmagent:chat' will not resolve. Prefer a model operation such as 'v/models/anthropic/claude-sonnet-5' for llmOperation. Legacy provider paths such as 'v/ops/langchain/anthropic' remain supported with an optional model override. Provider and model operations resolve API keys from the user's secret store via their default secretKey, or you can override with apiKey='s/<SECRET_NAME>'. After creation, send work via agent_request and inspect via agent_info.

agentId.description: Target agent reference: a bare human-readable name for the caller's namespace, g/<id>, /g/<id>, or <ownerDID>/g/<id>

config.description: One config layer, or an ordered array of additive layers. A layer is an inline map or a string reference resolving to a flat config map or an asset with agent.config. Later layers override earlier values; nested maps merge recursively, arrays replace. Null is not a layer; put null inside a map to clear an inherited field. References include workspace paths, asset refs, DID URLs, and venue templates. A resolved composition may include state, used as initial agent state.

operation.description: Transition operation for the agent — must be a resolvable lattice path (e.g. 'v/ops/llmagent/chat' for persona chat, 'v/ops/goaltree/chat' for goal-decomposing planners). Bare adapter shorthand like 'llmagent:chat' will NOT resolve. Determines how the agent processes tasks.

systemPrompt.description: System prompt defining the agent's role and behaviour: the text itself, or one context entry resolved once per cycle — {ref: 'w/prompts/x'} for a workspace path, {ref: 'dlfs/<drive>/<file>'} for a DLFS file, {op, input?} for a read-only operation that returns the text, {job} for a completed job's text output. An entry that does not resolve fails the cycle; create warns when it does not resolve now.

llmOperation.description: LLM operation path. Prefer a model operation such as v/models/anthropic/claude-sonnet-5; provider operations remain compatible. Keep this in a separate config layer so behavioural templates remain provider-neutral.

apiKey.description: Optional secret reference such as s/ANTHROPIC_API_KEY; the provider operation's default secret is used when absent.

tools.description: Exact tool selector. Entries are operation paths or {operation,name?,description?} maps; harness tools such as subgoal and context_load use bare names. A later tools array replaces an earlier one.

defaultTools.description: Opt into the built-in default tool pack — deliberately minimal, read-only workspace access (covia read/list) — on top of the declared tools. Defaults to false: the agent sees only its own 'tools' list. Capability tools (writes, agents, assets, grid, schema) arrive via skills (skill_load) or explicit 'tools' entries.

model.description: Optional LLM model name; the selected provider's default applies when absent.

caps.description: Capability restrictions — array of {with, can} objects limiting what the agent can access

accepts.description: Target-side admission (#447): who besides the owner may talk to this agent — agent:request/trigger (agent/request) and agent:message/chat/step (agent/message) — without a delegation. "owner" (default): nobody. "venue": the venue operator — the venue principal and the agents it owns, not every user hosted here. An array: exact principal DIDs — a user DID admits that user only, <userDID>:g:<agentId> admits that one agent only; "venue" may appear as an entry. No prefixes. Admission covers talking only: reads, updates and control still need a delegation. The public principal is never admitted (anonymous exposure remains a2a.public + a2a.caps). Malformed values are rejected.

context.description: Operator-pinned context entries: inline text, refs, job results, or read-only operation results. Entries are trusted system instructions by default; set trusted:false on data that must remain inside a pinned_context tool result.

loads.description: Operator-pinned live loads: a map of key to entry spec. The key is the reference (lattice path, skill path with {skill: true}) unless the spec declares its own source — {text}, {op, input?} (volatile by default: rendered in the tail, never cached), {job} — under any key. Non-skill entries are trusted system instructions by default; use trusted:false for reference data. Each value may also include label, budget, required, volatile, and contributed tools, skills and skillsets.

skills.description: Skill directory/reference sources used to build the live skills index.

oneOf.description: Reference to a config map or canonical agent asset stored in workspace, assets, or elsewhere
Ordered config layers, merged left-to-right with later values winning.

definition.description: Asset ID of an agent definition carrying the canonical agent.config facet. Retained for compatibility; new callers normally pass the asset reference as a config layer.

status.description: Current status of the agent: SLEEPING, RUNNING, SUSPENDED, or TERMINATED

warnings.description: Warnings relevant to agent creation. The agent WAS created — these are advisories about configuration that looks wrong, each a human-readable message to act on. Everything flagged is resolved live at run time, so fixing it takes effect without recreating the agent. Absent when there is nothing to flag.
